title_en: Liu Baochang v. Anhui Dongtai Textile Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of patent rights

full_text_en:
Liu Baochang v. Anhui Dongtai Textile Co., Ltd.

Dispute over Infringement of Patent Right

Ruling Summary

The scope of protection of an invention patent shall be determined by the content of its claims. All technical features recorded in the claims collectively define the scope of protection of the patent right. Therefore, only when the technical features of the accused infringing method are respectively identical or equivalent to all the technical features recorded in the claims can it be determined that the accused infringing method falls within the scope of protection of the patent right.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min San Jian Zi No. 46-1

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Liu Baochang, male, born in December 1948, Han ethnicity, retired employee of the former Anhui No. 2 Cotton Textile Mill, residing at No. 304, Building 3, Textile Second Village, Heping Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Anhui Dongtai Textile Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 97, Longquan West Road, Dianbu Town, Feidong County, Anhui Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Weiguo, Chairman.

Agent ad litem: Wei Shenghua, male, employee of Anhui Dongtai Textile Co., Ltd., residing at Textile New Village Dormitory, Dianbu Town, Feidong County, Anhui Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Fengsheng, lawyer of Anhui Ludong Law Firm.

With respect to the case of dispute over infringement of patent right between the Applicant for Retrial Liu Baochang and the Respondent Anhui Dongtai Textile Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongtai Company), the Anhui High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2006) Wan Min San Zhong Zi No. 0021 on December 5, 2006, which has become legally effective. On August 26, 2008, Liu Baochang filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

Liu Baochang applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. Under the premise that the patent in question is valid, it should be acknowledged that the patent in question is neither identical nor equivalent to the prior art, including the original shuttle changing adjustment method of automatic shuttle changing looms. Without adding or removing any parts of the loom, and with the machine structure, purpose, and operating principles unchanged, the patent in question achieves significant technological progress and has substantial economic value. Dongtai Company must use the patented method to meet the expected functional requirements. Since Dongtai Company did not apply for a declaration of invalidity of the patent right, it can be presumed that it used the patented method. 2. Under the condition that the machine structure, purpose, and operating principles of the automatic shuttle changing loom remain unchanged, as long as it can be proven that the automatic shuttle changing loom used by Dongtai Company has the same structure and purpose as those in the patent in question, it can be presumed that Dongtai Company necessarily used the patented method and infringed the patent right. The second instance judgment's finding that the original shuttle changing adjustment method of the automatic shuttle changing loom is neither identical nor equivalent to the patented method constitutes an error in fact-finding. 3. The Applicant for Retrial's acquisition of the patented method can prove that the prior art before the filing date, i.e., the original shuttle changing adjustment method of the automatic shuttle changing loom, could not meet the expected functional requirements of the machine, and the existing shuttle changing method is bound to be eliminated. The patented method is the only method to achieve the expected functional requirements without changing the traditional machine structure, etc., and Dongtai Company can only produce by using the patented method.

The Respondent Dongtai Company argued in its defense: 1. Liu Baochang's application for retrial has no factual basis. 2. The Respondent uses a method of adjusting shuttle changing with a three-purpose gauge. This method is a pre-existing method before the filing date of the patent in question, recorded in the reference book "Textile Preservation" compiled by the Henan Textile Administration Bureau. The photographs taken by the first instance court during evidence preservation can also prove this.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province (hereinafter referred to as the first instance court) found that: Liu Baochang filed a patent application with the State Intellectual Property Office on March 16, 2002, for an invention patent with patent number 02112782.4, titled "Method for Adjusting Shuttle Changing of Wooden Shuttles Applicable to Shuttle Looms Using Automatic Shuttle Changing Looms" (hereinafter referred to as the patent in question), which was granted on June 22, 2005. The patent in question contains two claims, where Claim 1 is an independent claim and Claim 2 is a dependent claim. Claim 1 includes the following technical features: A method for adjusting the shuttle changing of wooden shuttles applicable to shuttle looms using an automatic shuttle changing loom, characterized by: (1) When a V-shaped screw transmits power from the striking tongue to the pushing slider, and the pushing slider pushes the wooden shuttle used for the shuttle loom on the shuttle magazine foot from one side until the rear upper edge of the wooden shuttle is just pushed to the front edge of the front frog rail or the rear upper edge of the wooden shuttle has been pushed into a position 2 mm deep from the front edge of the front frog rail, first hold the wooden shuttle by hand, maintaining a close contact relationship between the bottom plane of the wooden shuttle and the plane of the shuttle guide surface of the shuttle magazine foot, then adjust the position of the movable shaft on the movable shaft support foot on the shuttle magazine, so that the horizontal vertical distance between the front edge of the front frog rail and the front convex edge plate, i.e., the horn mouth, is greater than the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle, and the horizontal vertical distance equals the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle plus a gap of 2 to 7 mm, so that the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle is positioned in the middle of the horn mouth; (2) When the front frog rail is fully raised, i.e., when the highest point of the wooden shuttle used for the shuttle loom is jammed between the front frog rail and the front convex edge plate, adjust the positions of the screws for the shuttle box raised back plate arm rods in the long and short arms of the shuttle box raised back plate respectively, so that the wire at the bottom of the shuttle box raised back plate is level with the plane of the shuttle box bottom plate, based on the middle straight part of the wire, with an error not exceeding ±1 mm; then adjust the degree of bending of the wire so that the wire at the bottom of the shuttle box raised back plate is parallel to the rear edge of the shuttle box bottom plate, with a gap between them being 1/3 to 1/4 of the width of the wooden shuttle.

On April 20, 2006, Liu Baochang filed a lawsuit with the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, alleging that: Dongtai Company, without permission, used the patented technology, infringing the plaintiff's patent right. He requested the court to order Dongtai Company to cease the infringement and compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 10,000. To support his claims, Liu Baochang submitted the following evidence to the first instance court: Evidence 1: copies of the patent certificate, patent specification, and receipts for annual fee payment of the patent in question, to prove that the plaintiff enjoys the patent right; Evidence 2: copies of the textile industry standards of the People's Republic of China "FZ/T94002-1991 (Shuttle Changing Type Wooden Shuttle)" and "FZ/T94021-95 (Shuttle Changing Cotton Loom)", to prove that the patent in question breaks through two industry standards and has the necessary conditions to become patented technology; Evidence 3: a copy of the cover and page 152 of "1515 Loom Repair Method", to prove that the defendant's current automatic shuttle changing adjustment method for the loom no longer has reason to be adjusted in this way; Evidence 4: a copy of the cover and pages 152 to 155 of the textbook "Loom", to explain the structure of the automatic shuttle changing mechanism of the loom; Evidence 5: based on Liu Baochang's application, the conversation record and five photographs taken on-site by the first instance court during evidence preservation in the Dongtai Company's weaving workshop, to prove that the defendant is using an automatic loom directly related to the patent in question to produce fabric.

Dongtai Company uses shuttle looms in production, and the automatic shuttle changing adjustment method it adopts includes the following steps: correcting the height position of the shuttle magazine foot, using a three-purpose gauge to check the distance between the two feet of the shuttle magazine and the shuttle box bottom plate. If the distance is incorrect, slightly loosen the nut of the shuttle magazine shaft, use the jaw of a wrench to hold the nut, and using the angle lever as a fulcrum, pry upward to move the shaft upward in the elongated hole of the support foot, or lightly tap the shuttle magazine shaft to move the shaft downward for adjustment.

The first instance court held that comparing the essential technical features recorded in the claims of the patent in question with the features of the accused infringing method, the adjustment method of the patent in question adjusts the distances and positions of relevant parts through the shuttle itself without adding or removing any parts of the loom or changing the original assembly specifications of the loom, whereas Dongtai Company uses a three-purpose gauge to adjust the spacing between the shuttle magazine foot and the shuttle box bottom plate. Therefore, the adjustment method used by Dongtai Company is neither identical nor equivalent to the patented method. The technical solution of Dongtai Company does not fall within the scope of protection of the claims of the patent in question and thus does not constitute infringement. Liu Baochang's claims lack factual and legal basis, cannot be established, and should be dismissed. Accordingly, the court dismissed Liu Baochang's claims.

Liu Baochang, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Anhui High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the second instance court). During the appeal, he submitted the following two pieces of evidence to the second instance court: Evidence 1: the book "Repair and Use of Shuttles" (First Edition, October 1992, Textile Industry Press), to prove that there is no difference between wooden shuttles and nylon shuttles; Evidence 2: the book "1511 Automatic Loom Maintenance Atlas" (Second Edition, October 1980, Textile Industry Press), to prove that Dongtai Company could not possibly use a three-purpose gauge for shuttle changing adjustment.

The second instance court held that the newly submitted evidence by Liu Baochang does not constitute new evidence as stipulated in Article 41(2) of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," and cannot achieve its purpose of proof. Therefore, the said evidence cannot be used as a basis for determining the facts of the case. Liu Baochang's claim based on the said evidence that Dongtai Company could not possibly use a three-purpose gauge for shuttle changing adjustment should not be accepted.

The second instance court divided Claim 1 of the patent in question into the following three technical features: "A. When a V-shaped screw transmits power from the striking tongue to the pushing slider, and the pushing slider pushes the wooden shuttle used for the shuttle loom on the shuttle magazine foot from one side until the rear upper edge of the wooden shuttle is just pushed to the front edge of the front frog rail or the rear upper edge of the wooden shuttle has been pushed into a position 2 mm deep from the front edge of the front frog rail, first hold the wooden shuttle by hand, maintaining a close contact relationship between the bottom plane of the wooden shuttle and the plane of the shuttle guide surface of the shuttle magazine foot, then adjust the position of the movable shaft on the movable shaft support foot on the shuttle magazine, so that the horizontal vertical distance between the front edge of the front frog rail and the front convex edge plate, i.e., the horn mouth, is greater than the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle, and the horizontal vertical distance equals the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle plus a gap of 2 to 7 mm, so that the width of the rear side of the wooden shuttle is positioned in the middle of the horn mouth; B. When the front frog rail is fully raised, i.e., when the highest point of the wooden shuttle used for the shuttle loom is jammed between the front frog rail and the front convex edge plate, adjust the positions of the screws for the shuttle box raised back plate arm rods in the long and short arms of the shuttle box raised back plate respectively, so that the wire at the bottom of the shuttle box raised back plate is level with the plane of the shuttle box bottom plate, based on the middle straight part of the wire, with an error not exceeding ±1 mm; C. Then adjust the degree of bending of the wire so that the wire at the bottom of the shuttle box raised back plate is parallel to the rear edge of the shuttle box bottom plate, with a gap between them being 1/3 to 1/4 of the width of the wooden shuttle."

The second instance court held that the patent in question is a method for adjusting the shuttle changing of wooden shuttles applicable to shuttle looms using automatic shuttle changing looms, and does not extend to products. The shuttle changing adjustment method is a complete technical solution composed of all the technical features recorded in Claim 1. The shuttle changing adjustment method used by Dongtai Company contains only one technical feature: using a three-purpose gauge to correct the height position of the shuttle magazine foot, i.e., using a three-purpose gauge to check the distance between the two feet of the shuttle magazine and the shuttle box bottom plate. If the distance is incorrect, slightly loosen the nut of the shuttle magazine shaft, use the jaw of a wrench to hold the nut, and using the angle lever as a fulcrum, pry upward to move the shaft upward in the elongated hole of the support foot, or lightly tap the shuttle magazine shaft to move the shaft downward for adjustment. Comparing the technical features of the shuttle changing adjustment method used by Dongtai Company with the essential technical features recorded in the claims of the patent in question, the former has only one technical feature, lacking the latter two technical features of the patented method, and the sole technical feature of the former is neither identical nor equivalent to technical feature A of the patent in question, with a qualitative difference between the two. The patent in question performs the shuttle changing adjustment by hand-holding the wooden shuttle without adding or removing any parts of the loom or changing the original assembly specifications. In contrast, Dongtai Company uses a three-purpose gauge to check and adjust the spacing between the shuttle magazine foot and the shuttle box bottom plate to achieve the purpose of shuttle changing adjustment. Therefore, the shuttle changing adjustment method used by Dongtai Company is neither identical nor equivalent to the patented method, does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question, and its actions do not infringe the patent right. Liu Baochang argued that Dongtai Company could not possibly use a three-purpose gauge for shuttle changing adjustment and must have used his patented method, but failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove this. Accordingly, the second instance court did not support Liu Baochang's appeal claims. The first instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed. Consequently, the second instance court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Upon review, this Court finds that the facts found by the first and second instance courts are true, and this Court confirms them.

This Court further finds that, based on Liu Baochang's application, the first instance court went to the Dongtai Company's weaving workshop on the afternoon of June 19, 2006, to prepare a conversation record and take five photographs. According to the conversation record, when responding to the judicial officer's questions regarding "Where did your shuttle changing method come from? What kind of shuttle changing method do you use?" the workshop director Chen Feng replied: "We use an automatic shuttle changing method introduced in the Textile Industry Press book 'Textile Preservation'." When responding to the judicial officer's question "Is the technology you use from the technical documentation accompanying the purchased equipment?" Chen Feng replied: "No technical documentation was provided with the equipment purchase. We use a three-purpose gauge to correct the height (distance) of N-16, N-17, then install the automatic part and other parts, and then use the three-purpose gauge to correct Q6, Q7. Liu Baochang uses a shuttle to adjust the movable shaft, we use a three-purpose gauge to adjust the movable shaft. We do not use the plaintiff's method, nor are we accustomed to it."

This Court holds that "he who asserts must prove" is the general rule for allocating the burden of proof in patent infringement dispute cases. The patent in question is a "method for adjusting shuttle changing of wooden shuttles applicable to shuttle looms using automatic shuttle changing looms," which does not involve product manufacturing and does not fall within the exception of reversed burden of proof applicable to new product manufacturing method patents under Article 57(2) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the patentee Liu Baochang bears the burden of proving that the shuttle changing adjustment method used by Dongtai Company falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question. If there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the patentee's factual claims, the patentee shall bear the adverse consequences. According to the facts found by this Court, although Liu Baochang submitted multiple pieces of evidence to the first and second instance courts in this case, only Evidence 5 submitted in the first instance proceedings relates to the shuttle changing adjustment method used by the accused infringer, Dongtai Company. According to the relevant content in the conversation record of Evidence 5, Dongtai Company uses a three-purpose gauge for shuttle changing adjustment. During the hearing of this Court, Liu Baochang explicitly acknowledged that if Dongtai Company uses a three-purpose gauge for shuttle changing adjustment, it is different from the patented method.

The scope of protection of an invention patent shall be determined by the content of its claims. All technical features recorded in the claims collectively define the scope of protection of the patent right. Therefore, only when the technical features of the accused infringing method are respectively identical or equivalent to all the technical features recorded in the claims can it be determined that the accused infringing method falls within the scope of protection of the patent right. In this case, Dongtai Company claimed that it uses a three-purpose gauge for the shuttle changing adjustment of the loom, and this method is not identical to step A of Claim 1. Therefore, the evidence provided by Liu Baochang is insufficient to prove that the shuttle changing adjustment method used by Dongtai Company includes technical features identical or equivalent to steps B and C of Claim 1, and cannot prove that the accused infringing method falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question.

Liu Baochang argued: "The Applicant for Retrial's acquisition of the patented method can prove that the prior art before the filing date could not meet the expected functional requirements of the machine, and the existing shuttle changing method is bound to be eliminated. Under the condition that the machine structure, purpose, and operating principles of the automatic shuttle changing loom remain unchanged, Dongtai Company can only produce by using the patented method." Clearly, this ground for retrial application cannot be established. The grant of a patent for the invention in question only proves that the patent in question meets the conditions for patent authorization under laws and regulations. It does not prove that the prior art before the filing date of the patent in question could not be implemented after the patent grant, nor does it prove that the patented method is the only method to achieve the expected functional requirements on an automatic shuttle changing loom. Therefore, the Applicant for Retrial's assertion that Dongtai Company necessarily used the patented technology after the patent grant is merely an inference, lacking factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the retrial application of the Applicant for Retrial Liu Baochang does not meet the circumstances stipulated in Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

To reject Liu Baochang's application for retrial.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang
Acting Judge: Li Jian
Acting Judge: Luo Xia

April 27, 2009

Clerk: Wang Xin
